item.title: Angry crowds rally against Slovakia's pro-Russian leader on Velvet Revolution anniversary
item.description:
Angry crowds rally against Slovakia's pro-Russian leader on Velvet Revolution anniversary
Crowds have gathered in Slovakia to protest the government of pro-Russian Prime Minister Robert Fico on the anniversary of the 1989 Velvet Revolution, which ended communist rule in CzechoslovakiaByThe Associated PressNovember 17, 2026, 1:50 PM
BRATISLAVA, Slovakia -- People in Slovakia took to the streets Tuesday to rally against the government of pro-Russian Prime Minister Robert Fico on the anniversary of the 1989 Velvet Revolution that brought an end to decades of communist rule in Czechoslovakia.
Opposition parties organized the protests in dozens of communities across the country, where Fico remains as Europe’s most pro-Russian leader since Hungary’s Viktor Orbán was ousted from power in April.
“We’ve had enough of Fico,” chanted people in Bratislava, where organizers estimated 25,000 gathered in the downtown SNP square. One banner had a message for the prime minister: “Go to hell.”
The capital's rally united the liberal groups Progressive Slovakia and the Democrats with pro-business Freedom and Solidarity, the conservative Christian Democrats and an alliance of ethnic Hungarians. Together they hope to defeat Fico and his coalition government in next year’s parliamentary election.
“Just as in 1989, what unites us must be stronger than what divides us,” said Michal Šimečka, leader of the major opposition Progressive Slovakia party. “We’ll win only if we stick together.”
The government angered opponents by sending Foreign Minister Juraj Blanár to Russia for talks about renewing economic cooperation and other ties between the two countries for the first time since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

item.title: Pope Leo’s envoy brings message of comfort and unity to Holy Land Christians
item.description:
Pope Leo’s envoy brings message of comfort and unity to Holy Land Christians
The Catholic cardinal who oversees care of the faithful in the Holy Land visited Jerusalem to convey Pope Leo XIV's presence during troubled times for ChristiansByGIOVANNA DELL'ORTO Associated PressNovember 17, 2026, 1:29 PM
JERUSALEM -- The Vatican cardinal who oversees care of the Catholic faithful in the Holy Land visited Jerusalem on Tuesday, saying he wanted to convey the presence of Pope Leo XIV during particularly troubled times for Christians in the region.
Cardinal Claudio Gugerotti, prefect of the Vatican’s Dicastery for the Eastern Churches, prayed before the Holy Edicule inside the Church of the Holy Sepulcher, which marks the site where Christians believe Jesus was buried and rose from the dead.
“Lord, you were here physically,” Gugerotti prayed. “Lord, give hope to the world.”
Leaders of other Christian denominations in Jerusalem listened intently. The incense-filled ceremony, with clergy in solemn robes, offered a show of unity in the basilica where they have sometimes tensely shared worship space in a unique arrangement dating to the 19th century.
Preceded by bagpipers, rows of Franciscan friars and a large cross, Gugerotti and other Christian leaders processed through the narrow stone alleyways of Jerusalem’s Old City to the centuries-old church.
Harassment of clergy and faithful there has been rising. A rare violent attack on a religious sister in April sent shock waves across Israel.
“We know we are not always welcome,” said Sister Marie Reine, a Catholic nun who joined the procession in her white habit. “But our presence can bring peace, too.”
Most of Israel’s Christians are Palestinians, who have been the target of heated rhetoric after Arab-led parties made historic gains in the national elections last month. And neighboring Jordan is reeling from an attack that killed nine worshippers during a service at a Greek Orthodox church.

item.title: 4 detained in North Macedonia for alleged Iran-backed assassination plot in Greece
item.description:
4 detained in North Macedonia for alleged Iran-backed assassination plot in Greece
Authorities in North Macedonia say four people have been detained for questioning over an alleged Iran-linked assassination plot in neighboring GreeceByThe Associated PressNovember 17, 2026, 10:33 AM
SKOPJE, North Macedonia -- Authorities in North Macedonia have detained four people for questioning over an alleged Iran-linked assassination plot in neighboring Greece, officials said Tuesday.
Bojan Hristovski, director of North Macedonia's domestic security agency, said Tuesday that the suspects are all Macedonian citizens, adding that a fifth person had also been questioned and a sixth remained wanted by the authorities.
Hristovski named one of the Iranian recruiters as Naji Sharifi Zindashti, who is wanted in the United States for allegedly operating a criminal network that targets Iranian dissidents and activists abroad.
He did not give details of the alleged target in Greece, and Greek authorities did not immediately comment on the announcement.

item.title: Thousands demonstrate in Haiti’s capital to praise Bukele and Salvadoran troops fighting gangs
item.description:
Thousands demonstrate in Haiti’s capital to praise Bukele and Salvadoran troops fighting gangs
Thousands of people in Haiti's capital and beyond are praising El Salvador’s president, Nayib Bukele, and his troops for fighting gangs in the countryByDÁNICA COTO Associated Press and EVENS SANON Associated PressNovember 17, 2026, 10:21 AM
PORT-AU-PRINCE, Haiti -- Thousands of people poured into the streets of Haiti’s capital and beyond on Tuesday to praise El Salvador’s president, Nayib Bukele, and his troops as they fight gangs in the troubled Caribbean country.
Many in the crowd raised their fists and some clutched Haitian flags and signs in favor of Bukele.
“Bukele is here to free us!” some shouted.
“Give them the drones and the dogs!” others yelled in reference to the explosive drones that have targeted areas controlled by powerful gangs and the newly unveiled robot dogs making their rounds in Port-au-Prince.
Last month, Bukele deployed some 2,500 troops to Haiti after four of their own came under attack on Oct. 18 and remain missing. Fighting between gangs and foreign forces backed by Haitian authorities has only increased since then as Haiti remains mired in violence, with more than 20,000 people killed in the past five years.
While chants of “Bukele!” are spreading across Haiti, experts warn there’s no long-term plan to keep the country safe once the Central American troops pull out.
“This enthusiasm…could turn into anger against the government if the troops withdraw,” said Diego Da Rin, an analyst with International Crisis Group.
The group published a report Tuesday based on more than 100 interviews with officials in Haiti and abroad that reveal government failures and missteps as it urged Haitian officials to develop a plan to prevent their country from imploding once international forces leave.

item.title: Iran-backed group warns Iraqi forces against entering its stronghold near Baghdad
item.description:
Iran-backed group warns Iraqi forces against entering its stronghold near Baghdad
Kataib Hezbollah, a powerful Iran-backed armed group, has vowed to confront Iraqi government forces if they enter its stronghold near BaghdadByQASSIM ABDUL-ZAHRA Associated PressNovember 17, 2026, 10:09 AM
JURF AL-SAKHAR, Iraq -- A powerful Iran-backed armed group in Iraq vowed on Tuesday to confront government forces if they try to enter its main stronghold near Baghdad, denying allegations that it is smuggling oil from the area.
The standoff between Kataib Hezbollah and Iraqi authorities is shaping up to be the first major test of the new government’s resolve to disarm nonstate armed groups.
Abu Taleb al-Saidi of Kataib Hezbollah made the comments a day after Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi said security forces would enter Jurf al-Sakhar, south of Baghdad in Babil province, later this week. Local media reported that the group had until Friday to leave.
Kataib Hezbollah, one of Iraq’s most powerful armed groups, wields considerable influence in Jurf al-Sakhar and has maintained an armed presence there for more than a decade.
The planned move by al-Zaidi is part of his push to disarm powerful Iran-backed groups by mid-2027. The move by both rival sides raises alarms of internal Shiite fighting that has been mostly avoided since the 2003 U.S.-led invasion that removed Saddam Hussein from power.
Two officials from Kataib Hezbollah told The Associated Press that Gen. Esmail Qaani, who heads the foreign wing of Iran’s Revolutionary Guard, arrived in Baghdad on Monday to take part in mediation to end the tension. The officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to comment publicly, gave no further details.

item.title: David Beckham sues after his fragrance is sold in gas stations and discount stores
item.description:
David Beckham sues after his fragrance is sold in gas stations and discount stores
David Beckham’s company is suing beauty group Coty for at least $41 million, alleging that sales of his perfumes in discount stores breached their licensing agreement and damaged his luxury brandByJILL LAWLESS Associated PressNovember 17, 2026, 8:07 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
LONDON -- A dispute over the sale of David Beckham perfumes has struck a sour note with the soccer star turned style icon.
Beckham’s commercial company is suing a beauty firm after his “luxury” fragrances were allegedly found for sale in discount stores and a gas station bargain bin.
DB Ventures has filed a claim in the New York Supreme Court against German beauty group Coty, which makes and distributes a range of Beckham-branded fragrances and toiletries. They include the Classic and Instinct lines and the eaux de toilette Intimately and Exquisite Leather.
The claim argues that Beckham’s “world-renowned global brand is synonymous with excellence and refinement,” and “David Beckham products are a symbol of everyday luxury.”
“Imagine, then, the shock and dismay experienced when DB Ventures discovered that David Beckham products were being offered for sale in a gas station,” the legal document says. “How could this possibly have happened? Desperation and greed.”
Lawyers for DB Ventures allege that Beckham-branded products “ended up in the bargain bin inside a gas station” and at British budget retailer Poundland, “allowing the product to be sold for dollar store prices and associating the David Beckham brand with cheap, discount products.”
DB Ventures is seeking at least $41 million in damages for breach of its licensing agreement.

item.title: How Europe decided on 'return hubs' for migrants
item.description:
How Europe decided on 'return hubs' for migrants
A group of European countries has announced plans to establish a "migrant hub" in Rwanda for rejected asylum-seekersBySAM MCNEIL Associated Press and CLAUDIA CIOBANU Associated PressNovember 17, 2026, 7:02 AM
BRUSSELS -- A group of European countries announced on Monday that they aim to set up a “migrant hub” in Rwanda where rejected asylum-seekers could be sent from next year.
The European Union has worked for years to tighten migration rules, push down the number of asylum-seekers coming to the 27-nation bloc and increase deportations of migrants who aren’t entitled to stay. Sending people to centers outside Europe has emerged as a central element.
Here's a timeline of events that led to this agreement:
2015: Over 1 million people — the majority from war-stricken Syria — arrive in Europe seeking asylum, in what was at the time the largest migration crisis impacting the continent since World War II.
June 2016: The U.K. votes to leave the European Union in a referendum following a campaign during which those favoring Brexit use images of lines of migrants as a warning of what staying in the EU would entail.
September 2018: Sweden joins Europe's move to the right as voters boost a party that campaigned on anti-migrant sentiment and policies. It follows similar shifts in Germany, Austria and Italy as part of a backlash to the 2015 migration crisis. Denmark floats an idea it later scraps to deport migrants to a remote island once used as a research laboratory for contagious animal diseases.
September 2020: Denmark appoints a special envoy to toughen EU migration policies including setting up migrant reception centers in one or more countries outside the EU to diminish the incentive for migrants to seek asylum in Denmark and improving the deportation of rejected asylum-seekers.

item.title: Another commercial vessel sinks off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast
item.description:
Another commercial vessel sinks off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast
The Bulgarian Defense Ministry says that a Liberia-flagged gas tanker sank in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone in the Black SeaByThe Associated PressNovember 17, 2026, 6:40 AM
Share
SOFIA, Bulgaria -- A Liberia-flagged gas tanker sank in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea on Tuesday, according to the Defense Ministry.
Bulgarian military personnel and aircraft are involved in the search and rescue operation for the crew of 19 Filipino citizens of the gas carrier GAS HUSKY, which sank about 50 nautical miles (nearly 60 miles or 100 kilometers) off the coast, the ministry said in a statement.
It said that a Cougar chopper has been dispatched to the site where a life raft with people had been located. The rescue operation is ongoing.
The tanker had disappeared from radar shortly after midnight, and at 8:02 a.m. the emergency buoy was activated, emitting a signal for a sunken ship.
The tanker, en route from Alexandria, Egypt, to the Romanian port of Midia, is the second merchant ship to sink off Bulgaria’s coast in two days.

Investigations into the causes of the incidents are being launched. So far, there is no official information on whether the vessels were hit by drones.

item.title: EU-backed court convicts Kosovo ex-President of attempting to obstruct justice
item.description:
EU-backed court convicts Kosovo ex-President of attempting to obstruct justice
A European Union-backed court has convicted Kosovo's former president, Hashim Thaci, of trying to obstruct justice and contempt of courtByMIKE CORDER Associated PressNovember 17, 2026, 6:09 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
THE HAGUE, Netherlands -- A European Union-backed court on Tuesday convicted Kosovo's former president, Hashim Thaci, of charges that include trying to obstruct justice and contempt of court.
Thaci was sentenced to 17 months in prison to be added to a 25-year war crimes sentence that he's already serving.
It was the latest legal setback for Thaci, who was convicted in September along with three other former leaders of the Kosovo Liberation Army of committing war crimes during Kosovo's war for independence from Serbia in 1998-99. In that trial, Thaci was sentenced to 25 years in prison. His lawyer, Luka Misetic, said on X that he would appeal.
After Judge Christopher Gosnell of Canada read out the verdicts and sentence Tuesday, Thaci took off a headset that provides simultaneous interpretation and said: “This is politics, not justice.”
Kimberly West, the prosecutor who brings cases to the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, a special branch of the Kosovo legal system based in The Hague, welcomed the verdicts. She said they “send a clear message: those who attempt to subvert the rule of law, reveal confidential court materials or interfere with witnesses will be held accountable, no matter their status or position.”
Thaci resigned from office nearly six years ago to defend himself against the war crimes charges. He's still considered a war hero among his supporters in Kosovo, who angrily denounced his sentence in September. At the time, Kosovo Foreign Minister Glauk Konjufca condemned the verdicts as “a terrible judgment for Kosovo, for our people and for our liberation war.”

item.title: Military jet crashes in Serbia and the pilot is killed, authorities say
item.description:
Military jet crashes in Serbia and the pilot is killed, authorities say
Serbia's defense ministry says that a military jet crashed northwest of Belgrade, killing the pilotByThe Associated PressNovember 17, 2026, 5:07 AM
Share
BELGRADE, Serbia -- A Serbian military jet crashed on Tuesday northwest of Belgrade, killing the pilot, the defense ministry said. The ministry did not immediately give a reason for the crash.
The MIG-29 jet crashed around 8:45 a.m. into a field near the town of Stara Pazova, some 50 kilometers (30 miles) from the Serbian capital, a statement said.
Some local Serbian media published photos of the burning wreckage in the field and an ambulance and police cars parked nearby.
